prompt_provenance.note: Built between 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-23 in Claude Code sessions at ~/python/dota-analyst, whose transcripts no longer exist (transcripts older than 30 days are cleaned up; only MCP log caches remain). The empty clarification list is not evidence that there were none. The scripts were never committed. Scope and runs below are inferred from the scripts' docstrings and recovered from the saved outputs, which are evidence of what was run.

interpreted_question.text: Across The International 2026: which heroes were picked, banned and contested, how did teams and players perform, and, for upcoming series, each team's hero pools, the contested pool by position, and first-phase ban predictions (draft-board pages).
interpreted_question.provenance: Inferred from the four scripts' docstrings and the saved outputs.

implemented_scope.tournament: The International 2026 (TI15), Shanghai, 2026-08-13..08-23, patch 7.41e, 16 teams; Stratz leagueId 19719
implemented_scope.discovery: league(id: 19719) is null in Stratz, so matches are found by crawling player(steamAccountId).matches(request: {leagueId: 19719}) from one participant to closure, then fetched one id at a time with match(id:) (see ti2026_fetch.py)
implemented_scope.report_grain: heroes: picks, wins, bans (split by draft phase), contest; teams: series and game records; players: one row per player slot
implemented_scope.scouting_grain: one row per player per hero in chronological order; with two teams, the contested pool overall and by each hero's modal tournament position, and a first-phase ban prediction

methodological_choices: A pick is one player slot; a ban is a pickBans row with isPick = false; contest = picks + bans, over games.
Draft phases are taken from pickBans.order: phase 1 = slots 0-6, phase 2 = 9-11, phase 3 = 18-21.
A series is grouped on seriesId; its winner is the team with more game wins.
Scouting assigns each hero the position it was most played at across the whole tournament; heroes whose modal position holds under 60% of their games are marked flex.

Ban prediction is a transparent blend, not a model. Without --series: 45% tournament first-phase ban rate, 35% the banning team's own rate, 20% opponent threat. With --series: in-series bans 40%, tournament 25%, own 20%, threat 15%.
Stratz reports registered org names; --aliases labels teams by the name they played under (PARIVISION as TEAM VISION, BetBoom Team as BoomBoys).

rerun.requirements: The report and scouting read only the cached match JSON (the heroes constant is fetched once with a 10-year TTL). The fetch needs STRATZ_TOKEN and network access.
rerun.repeatability_note: Finished matches don't change, so reruns against the 146-match cache reproduce the recorded numbers. That cache stops before game 5 of the grand final; a --refresh fetch would add it and change the report. The two 2026-08-22 scouting runs used a 139-match cache and an earlier version of ti2026_scouting.py, so they can't be reproduced; their outputs in out/ are the record.
